exam.title: Design and Technology Paper 1 (17/1) - October/November 2024
exam.subject: Design and Technology
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following injuries requires the application of an ice pack when giving first aid?
questions.explanation: An ice pack narrows the blood vessels under the skin, which reduces the swelling and bleeding into the tissue that cause a bruise. Cuts and abrasions need cleaning and a dressing, and a person in shock needs to be kept warm, not cooled.

questions.question: Which of the following warning signs shows chemical hazard?
questions.explanation: The skull and crossbones warns of a toxic (poisonous) chemical. The exclamation mark is a general warning, the trefoil warns of radiation, and the lightning flash warns of electricity.

questions.question: Which of the following plastics can be reheated and reshaped many times without changing its structure and properties?
questions.explanation: Polythene is a thermoplastic: it softens when heated and can be reshaped again and again. Polyester resin, urea formaldehyde and phenol formaldehyde are thermosetting plastics, which set permanently once cured.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is used for making ringing bells?
questions.explanation: Bells are cast from bronze (an alloy of copper and tin, often called bell metal) because it is hard, resists corrosion and rings with a clear, lasting tone.

questions.question: Which of the following constructions is the correct method of dividing line EY into 5 equal parts?
questions.explanation: Draw a construction line from E, step off five equal divisions along it, join the last division to Y, then draw lines parallel to that join back onto EY. The arrows in A show the divisions being projected back onto EY. In B the arrows point onto the construction line instead, C marks both lines, and D has no projection marks at all.

questions.question: Read this description: "A rubber-based adhesive which is waterproof and can be used to join vinyl, leather, cardboard and other various laminates." Which of the following adhesives is described?
questions.explanation: Contact glue (contact adhesive) is rubber based and waterproof. It is spread on both surfaces, left until touch-dry and then pressed together, which suits flexible sheets such as vinyl, leather and laminates.

questions.question: The figure shows a wooden step used by a Design and Technology teacher. Which manufactured board can be used to make the top of the step?
questions.explanation: Plywood is made of thin veneers glued with the grain of each layer at right angles to the next, which makes it strong and stiff in every direction and able to carry a person standing on it. The layered edge shown in the figure is typical of plywood. Hardboard is too thin and weak, and chipboard is weak when loaded and if it gets damp.

questions.question: The figure shows a wooden step used by a Design and Technology teacher. Which of the following abrasives is suitable for smoothening the surface and edges of the step?
questions.explanation: Glass paper is the abrasive made for wood. Emery cloth and wet and dry paper are used on metals and plastics, and steel wool is mostly used between coats of finish.

questions.question: The figure shows a wooden step used by a Design and Technology teacher. Which of the following is suitable to finish the top of the step?
questions.explanation: Clear varnish forms a hard, durable, waterproof film that stands up to being walked on while still showing the grain of the wood. Wax polish would make the top slippery and wears off quickly, and linseed oil gives little protection against wear.

questions.question: The figure shows a wooden step used by a Design and Technology teacher. Which fabrication method is suitable for joining the frame at K?
questions.explanation: K is where a rail meets the upright of the frame. A mortise and tenon joint is the standard strong joint for joining a rail to a leg in a frame, because the tenon is glued deep into the mortise and resists racking.

questions.question: Which of the following can be considered when analysing the design theme?
questions.explanation: The design process starts from a broad theme. Analysing the theme means looking at the different situations within it, and a problem is then identified within one of those situations before a brief is written.

questions.question: Which mechanism will allow the lid to open when the pedal is pressed in the diagram below?
questions.explanation: Pressing the pedal down makes the linkage push the rod up, so the output moves in the opposite direction to the input. A linkage that reverses the direction of motion is a reverse motion linkage, as used in a pedal bin.

questions.question: Which of the following software is the most suitable when enhancing drawings?
questions.explanation: Photoshop is image-editing software, used to enhance an existing drawing or image by adjusting colour, tone, shading and effects. CorelDRAW and Illustrator are mainly for creating vector drawings, and Rhinoceros is 3D modelling software.

questions.question: At which stage of the design process is the generation of a variety of solutions to solve an identified problem?
questions.explanation: Exploration of ideas (generating possible solutions) is where a range of different ideas is sketched. The best one is then refined at the development stage.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is shown by the figure below?
questions.explanation: The figure is made of thin members joined at their ends, so it is a frame structure. Triangulation is a way of strengthening a frame, not a type of structure; a shell is a thin outer skin and a mass structure is solid material.

questions.question: Which of the following terms refers to the study of a person in relation to their work and environment?
questions.explanation: Ergonomics is the study of how people interact with the things and spaces they use, so products can be designed to be comfortable, safe and efficient. Anthropometrics is the collection of body measurements used in ergonomics.

questions.question: Which of the following is a basic component of electricity?
questions.explanation: Current, voltage and resistance are the basic quantities that make up electricity. A bulb, a cable and a switch are components of a circuit rather than of electricity itself.

questions.question: What is the function of the electronic component shown below?
questions.explanation: The component is a transistor in a metal can with three legs (emitter, base and collector). In school circuits it is used as an electronic switch: a small current into the base switches on a larger current through the collector.

questions.question: When evaluating an artefact, one should always refer to the
questions.explanation: Evaluation checks the finished product against the specification, the list of requirements it was designed to meet.

questions.question: The diagram shows a boring bit. What is the name of the bit?
questions.explanation: The adjustable cutter held by a screw is the feature of an expansive (expansion) bit. The cutter slides out or in to bore holes of different sizes with one bit.

questions.question: The diagram shows a boring bit. Which of the following is an advantage when the bit is in use?
options: It is used on all drill machines.
It is used to drill holes of different depths.
It is used to bore holes of different diameters.
It is used on machines with low and high speeds.
questions.explanation: Because its cutter can be set to different positions, one expansive bit bores holes of a range of diameters, saving the cost of a set of fixed-size bits.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a factor in determining the cost of a product?
questions.explanation: The cost of a product is worked out from the cost of materials, labour and overheads, with the profit added on top to give the price. Demand, advertising and market research affect sales rather than how the cost is calculated.

questions.question: The diagram shows a wall-mounted suggestion box made of aluminium. Which of the following hinges can be used to fit the lid to the main body?
questions.explanation: A piano (continuous) hinge runs the full length of the joint, so it supports a thin metal lid along its whole edge and keeps it from bending. It is easily riveted or screwed to thin aluminium sheet.

questions.question: The diagram shows a wall-mounted suggestion box made of aluminium. Which of the following is the correct order of steps when making the slot?
questions.explanation: The slot is measured, then marked out on the metal, then cut, and the cut edges are finished last.

questions.question: The diagram shows a wall-mounted suggestion box made of aluminium. What is the name of the fitting labelled P?
questions.explanation: P is a hasp and staple: a hinged plate on the lid with a slot that fits over a loop (the staple) on the body, so a padlock can lock the box.

questions.question: The diagram illustrates a deforming process. Which deforming process is illustrated by the diagram?
questions.explanation: A pre-heated sheet is placed over a mould and a press tool (the plug) is brought down to squeeze it into shape. Forming a sheet between a mould and a press tool is press forming.

questions.question: Which of the following electronic symbols represents a Light Dependent Resistor?
questions.explanation: The LDR symbol is a resistor (rectangle) inside a circle with arrows pointing in to show light falling on it. A is a microphone, B a motor and D a lamp.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pure metal?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a pure metal, a single element. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, and cast iron and mild steel are iron with carbon.

questions.question: The term Energy Conservation refers to the practice of using
questions.explanation: Energy conservation means using less energy, for example by switching off appliances and using efficient ones, so that resources last longer and less is wasted.

questions.question: Use the hand saws shown. Which of the hand saws shown is used to make large holes in panels?
questions.explanation: Saw (ii) is a pad (keyhole or compass) saw. Its narrow, tapered blade fits into a drilled hole so it can cut out a large hole in the middle of a panel. (i) is a handsaw, (iii) a tenon saw and (iv) a coping saw.

questions.question: Use the hand saws shown. Which of the hand saws shown is a back saw?
questions.explanation: Saw (iii) is a tenon saw, a back saw: the heavy strip along the top of the blade keeps it stiff for accurate straight cuts.

questions.question: Expanded polystyrene can also be used as food containers because it is
questions.explanation: A material that touches food must be safe to eat from. Expanded polystyrene is non-toxic, and it also insulates well, keeping food hot or cold.

questions.question: Which of the following tools is used for marking various angles on a resistant material?
questions.explanation: A sliding bevel has a blade that can be set and locked at any angle. A try square only marks 90°, a mitre square only 45°, and a combination square 90° and 45°.

questions.question: The diagram shows a 3D presentation and 2D working drawings of a product. What is the name given to view K?
questions.explanation: View K shows the product cut through, with the cut surfaces hatched with diagonal lines. A hatched view of a cut is a sectional view.

questions.question: The diagram shows a 3D presentation and 2D working drawings of a product. Which of the following is improperly dimensioned?
questions.explanation: Vertical dimensions should read from the right-hand side of the drawing, with the figures running from bottom to top, as the 50 does. The 100 is written the other way round, so it reads from the left.

questions.question: Which of the diagrams shown below is transparent?
questions.explanation: In D the back edges of the block can be seen through the front faces, together with short reflection marks. Being able to see the hidden edges is how a transparent material is shown. A and B show textured, grained materials, and C shows only its front faces.

questions.question: The diagram shows a Design and Technology teacher chiselling a piece of wood. Which chiselling method is shown in the diagram?
questions.explanation: The chisel is held upright and struck with a mallet to cut down across the grain. Driving the chisel with a mallet like this is vertical chopping; paring is done by hand pressure alone.

questions.question: The diagram shows a Design and Technology teacher chiselling a piece of wood. Which striking tool is being used in the diagram?
questions.explanation: The square-headed mallet is a wooden (carpenter's) mallet, used to strike wooden-handled chisels. Bossing and rawhide mallets are used on sheet metal, and rubber mallets for assembling work.

questions.question: How does a ceiling fan keep a room cool in summer period?
options: By sucking air out of the room
By moving air in a linear direction
By blowing air in backward direction
By drawing air in an oscillating motion
questions.explanation: A ceiling fan pushes a steady stream of air straight down into the room. The moving air carries heat and sweat away from the skin, so people feel cooler.

questions.question: Which of the following statements demonstrates torsion?
options: Twisting of an object at the ends
questions.explanation: Torsion is a twisting force, as when the ends of an object are turned in opposite directions, for example wringing a cloth or turning a screwdriver.
